label: 4bis
title: Saying No
subtitle: Hidden Brain, How To Say No

entries.d: to be so busy, with so many tasks or responsibilities, that you cannot take on anything else
x: I'd love to join the committee, but I already [[have my plate full]] this semester.

entries.d: to be very annoyed with yourself because you made a mistake or a bad decision
x: She [[kicked herself]] for saying yes when she really wanted to say no.

entries.t: out of the goodness of your heart
entries.d: because you are kind and generous, without expecting anything in return
x: I ran across town to pick up her groceries [[out of the goodness of my heart]].

entries.d: to relax, especially by sitting or lying comfortably
x: While I was carrying the shopping, her husband was [[kicking back]] in the garden with a beer.

entries.d: to force someone to answer or decide immediately, in a way that makes them uncomfortable
x: Being asked in front of the whole team really [[put me on the spot]].

entries.d: you suddenly feel disappointed or worried because of bad news or an unwelcome request
x: When the stranger asked for my aisle seat, my [[heart sank]].

entries.d: to make a special effort to do something, even when it is inconvenient
x: People will [[go out of their way]] to say yes, even to strangers, because saying no feels so hard.
Some requests are completely [[out of line]], yet people still agree to them.

entries.d: to refuse an offer, invitation, or request
x: It is much easier to [[turn down]] a request when nobody is watching you.

entries.d: to make great efforts to achieve something
x: We [[strive to]] create a good impression in other people's minds.

entries.d: to be essentially the result of one main factor, once everything has been considered
x: Why women say yes more often [[boils down to]] social expectations of helpfulness.

entries.d: without careful thought or planning; randomly, in an uncontrolled way
x: I don't say no [[willy-nilly]]: I'm very thoughtful about what I commit to.

entries.d: so shocked or stunned by something unexpected that you cannot react normally
x: When my boss told me to wait for the fax, I was [[shell-shocked]].

entries.d: extremely surprised, so much that you hardly know what to say
x: I was [[flabbergasted]] when my nine-year-old explained the acquaintance trap to me.

entries.d: feeling bitter and angry because you think you have been treated unfairly
x: Saying yes when you want to say no often leaves you [[resentful]] towards the other person.

entries.d: to make someone less angry or upset by giving them something or agreeing with them
x: He said yes just to [[placate]] his friend, even though the request was unreasonable.

entries.d: to destroy something completely, especially hopes, plans, or confidence; literally, to break into small pieces
x: That one instruction [[shattered]] my plans for the evening.

speaking.q: Tell me about a time you said yes when you wanted to say no. How did you feel afterwards?
Why do you think it is so hard to turn down a request from someone you barely know?
Have you ever been put on the spot by a boss or a colleague? What did you say?
Should we always help others out of the goodness of our hearts, or is it healthy to say no sometimes? Where would you draw the line?
Describe a moment when something unexpected shattered your plans. How did you react?
